actions.text: ASSUMING FIRST SPONSORSHIP - Mr. LaHood asked unanimous consent that he may hereafter be considered as the first sponsor of H.R. 2424, a bill originally introduced by Representative LaMalfa, for the purpose of adding cosponsors and requesting reprintings pursuant to clause 7 of rule XII. Agreed to without objection.
Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

dimensions.assessment: Affects purchasers, manufacturers, suppliers, dealerships, and operators of heavy-duty trucks, trailers, and tractors across the United States.
dimensions.evidence: in 2020, there were approximately 1,300,000 United States manufacturing, supplier, dealership, and heavy-duty trucking and trailer related jobs

dimensions.assessment: Eliminates a 12% retail excise tax that adds thousands of dollars (up to $50,000) to the cost of new heavy vehicles.
dimensions.evidence: adds $7,000 or more to the cost of new trailers, $20,000 or more for new clean diesel trucks, and as much as $50,000 to the next generation of trucks

dimensions.assessment: Repeals a major federal ad valorem tax source that provides revenue to the Highway Trust Fund.
dimensions.evidence: receipts from the tax deposited in the Highway Trust Fund can vary greatly... repeals subchapter C

dimensions.assessment: Makes extensive structural amendments to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, including repealing subchapter C of chapter 31 and enacting conforming amendments.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 31 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by striking subchapter C

dimensions.assessment: Permanent tax repeal applying to sales and installations on or after the date of introduction.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to sales and installations on or after the date of the introduction of this Act.

missing_information: Exact annual revenue loss to the Highway Trust Fund resulting from the repeal
importance_detail.rationale: The bill repeals the 12% federal retail excise tax on heavy trucks, trailers, and tractors, altering tax collections deposited into the Highway Trust Fund.

summary: The Modern, Clean, and Safe Trucks Act of 2025 repeals the 12% federal retail excise tax currently imposed on the first retail sale of certain heavy trucks, trailers, tractors, and related chassis. The bill aims to lower the upfront costs of purchasing new heavy-duty vehicles, encourage the replacement of older high-emission vehicles, and remove tax burdens that disproportionately affect electric and alternative-fueled trucks.

affected_groups.effect: Will no longer pay the 12% federal retail excise tax upon purchasing new vehicles, which can reduce purchase costs by thousands of dollars.
affected_groups.group: Purchasers and operators of heavy-duty trucks, tractors, and trailers

affected_groups.effect: Face altered tax compliance rules regarding first retail sales of heavy commercial vehicles and potential changes in vehicle demand.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers, suppliers, and dealerships of heavy-duty trucks and trailers

affected_groups.effect: Loses the revenue collected from the 12% retail excise tax on heavy trucks and trailers, which previously supported surface transportation projects.

key_provisions: Repeals the 12% federal retail excise tax on heavy trucks, trailers, tractors, and related bodies and chassis.
Makes conforming amendments to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to remove references to the repealed tax and update definitions related to highway vehicle tires.
Removes tax revenue deposits from this specific retail excise tax out of the Highway Trust Fund.
Applies the repeal to sales and installations on or after the date the bill was introduced, March 27, 2025.
missing_information: The exact financial impact in dollars on the Highway Trust Fund's total budget.
Any proposed alternative revenue source to replace the funds lost by the Highway Trust Fund due to the excise tax repeal.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Modern, Clean, and Safe Trucks Act of 2025 repeals the 12% federal retail excise tax currently imposed on the first retail sale of certain heavy trucks, trailers, tractors, and related chassis. The bill aims to lower the upfront costs of purchasing new heavy-duty vehicles, encourage the replacement of older high-emission vehicles, and remove tax burdens that disproportionately affect electric and alternative-fueled trucks.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation addresses vehicle replacement incentives in the heavy-duty transportation sector by attempting to remove a tax that adds between $7,000 and $50,000 to new trucks and trailers. While the text notes that the tax provides variable revenue for the Highway Trust Fund, it does not specify an alternative funding mechanism to replace those lost revenues.
